title: The Readout Sheet
summary: The red plane keeps round 2's separate doors, and round 1's solid paper object comes back as a printed audit sheet. It shows phase 01 of the four, the big red 10, what the audit asks of you, what happens after, and a foot rule marked in ten working days.
story: It is the decision: 'Sound like you?' answers the two ledgers above it, the button asks once, and the sheet shows phase 01 from the method as a small, fixed first step that you keep either way. After it comes only the footer's index.
motion: Standalone (plays on load, at rest by about 2.1s): the label fades in, 'Request the' rises out of its mask, and the lighter 'System Audit.' follows. The paper rule draws, then the lede rises. At 0.7s the two doors and the path line rise together, so the button is in place before anything else arrives.

Then the sheet. Four registration marks appear around an empty frame (0.76 to 1.24s). The sheet then rises into that frame from its own bottom edge, like a page fed out of a printer (0.8s). Once it has landed, its ten day ticks ink in from the foot rule, left to right, 40ms apart. Nothing counts, nothing loops and nothing changes from dashed to solid.

Interaction: only the doors respond. The paper button warms to blush and its ↗ nudges; the contact link's underline brightens and its → nudges. With the keyboard, each door shows a paper focus ring. The sheet has no link, no hover state, no pointer cursor and no arrow, and the Tab key passes over it.
On the live page: the same sequence plays once, when the red plane scrolls into view. With reduced motion, the finished state shows at once, and there is no script at all.
addressed: Your note: round 1 felt 'more engaging, more well-thought-out, more proprietary-looking', and you asked for a middle ground. The solid paper object with the big red 10 and 'Phase 01 of 04 · Diagnose' is back. Round 2's separate button and contact link stay exactly where you approved them, and they arrive first.

The object is now a document, not a button and not the logo's square. It is a printed audit sheet, with registration marks at its corners and a paper margin all round. Its mono header sits over a rule in four segments, with only phase 01 printed solid (the same plan as the method's track). Below that are the red 10, three printed rows, and a foot rule marked in ten working days, from 01 Kickoff to Readout 10. You can't click it, so it never competes with 'Request a System Audit'.
The order stays clear. The headline comes first, then the paper button, which is the brightest object on the red. The sheet comes after, on a slightly warmer paper.

It says what the audit asks of you (two sessions, read-only CRM access) and what happens after you click (three questions, a 30-minute call with the founding team, then Day 01). It also gives the risk reverser: if not, the plan is still yours.
One quiet touch joins the two halves: 'Day 01.' at the end of the path line sits on the same baseline as '01 Kickoff' at the foot of the sheet.
notes: needs founder sign-off (D8): the '10' (ten working days), 'Two sessions' and 'read-only CRM access' are the current [EDIT ME] values in AuditSpec. There is no fee line until D8 chooses a fee posture. D5: 'Initiate' is retired for 'Request'. D7: the 'Deployment window open' chip is off this plane. Geometry (Swiss skin, 1440 stage): the section is 886px tall, with 160px top and bottom padding. The statement is 112px (.ac-statement--xl), held at 227px on whole pixels, in cols 1–8. The lede is in cols 1–6. The doors and the path line are in the doors position. The .ac-head grid is used here only to place the 112px statement and its doors, as STORY's build brief asks. It is not the standard 88px head, so the three-head budget is unchanged. The sheet is 280×396 (1:1.414), with its right edge on the page margin. Its top edge sits on the cap height of 'System Audit.' (y 346). Its foot line ('01 Kickoff · Readout 10') shares the path line's baseline (y 720), which puts the path line 47px under the doors. Inside the sheet: 18px paper margin on all four sides. The 12px mono header sits over a four-segment rule: phase 01 is a 2px ink bar, phases 02–04 are hairlines, and none of it is red. The 10 is .ac-num at 128px in --accent. 'working days, kickoff to readout' (15px) sits beside it, with its last line on the numeral's baseline. Three rows follow, each with an 11px mono key above a 14px value, divided by hairlines. The sheet's last rule is an ink hairline marked in ten days. Ten ticks hang from it: 01 and 10 at 9px, the eight days between at 5px, on a 27px pitch so every tick is crisp. Beneath them are 12px mono end values with the 14px words Kickoff and Readout. Fill: the light surface's --panel paper, a shade under the button's paper. Red: the plane only, plus red ink on paper objects (the button text and the 10). The label square, rule, registration marks and focus rings invert to paper. Departures from STORY's sheet spec, forced by its size: STORY's content needs about 440px at the stated sizes, but its two alignment rules leave 396. So the 10 is 128px (not 144), the row values are 14px (not 15), the unit sits beside the 10 rather than beneath it, and the margin is 18px (not 24). At 24px the value 'Two sessions, read-only CRM access' breaks onto two lines and the rows no longer fit. Kelwin comparison skin: Inter sets wider, so the sheet grows to about 412px. It grows upward, keeping its foot on the path baseline, so there its top sits about 16px above the cap line. text-wrap: pretty keeps 'CRM access' together on one line. ≤760px: one column, 16px gutters and a 52px statement. The doors wrap, and the sheet follows the path line at up to 280px wide. Checked at 390px with no horizontal scroll. No JS: everything is CSS keyed off .is-play. Tested stitched between fit and footer (home-cta.html): all three play, with no errors.
